verdict.rationale: The current npm release of @babylonjs/core is published under the permissive Apache-2.0 license, and the docs describe Babylon.js as an "open game and rendering engine." That means there are no per-title fees or royalties that could be repriced for shipped games. However, the pack has no evidence of the license's history over time or of any commitment against retroactive changes. Community praise for API backwards compatibility is about code, not licensing, so it does not count here. missing for 10: documented license/pricing history showing no changes, an explicit vendor policy against retroactive license changes, independent corroboration of licensing stability.

support.subject: As a studio lead, the pricing and license terms have a track record of stability — no retroactive changes that reprice games already shipped
